newsitem.title: GREECE: Short end of Greek yield curve firms in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Short end of Greek yield curve firms in late trade.

text.p: Greek money rates and forex forwards were firmer in late dealings and dealers attributed the pick up in rates to the closing out of positions from abroad.

"Shorts in depos and forex forwards trade five to 20 basis points higher on demand for funds from abroad," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Obviously, some players seek to close out positions for clients."
The central bank drained overnight cash at 12.40 percent but dealers said surplus liquidity was negligible.
Traders said they did not expect to hear anything new from the newly-elected premier's policy speech tonight.

They expected general statements and a renewed commitment to meeting Maastricht criteria in Simitis's statements to parliament tonight but they would listen carefully for possible changes in tax laws affecting financial products and the mutual fund industry.

Simitis, who took over as prime minister in January, was elected to a four-year term in early elections this month. His Panhellenic Socialist Movement (PASOK) has 162 deputies in the 300-seat parliament.
The mark was quoted at 157.00/05 drachmas from Wednesday's 156.990 fix, the dollar at 240.17/22 drachmas from 240.300 and the Ecu at 300.43/53 from 300.450 drachmas.
"There was two-way trade and about 52 million ecus were sold for drachmas at the fixing," said a dealer at a state bank.
